selectionRule: A public-ready entry carries an exact semantic source and every supporting file declared for this projection.

skills.name: bounded-support-routing
skills.description: Composes a finite support packet with an explicit action mode, observable return, and stopping event. Applies when a focused solution, implementation, or recovery route needs clear expectations, bounded attention, and a natural handback.

skills.name: collaboration-accounting
skills.description: Accounts for decision-changing collaboration observations and routes them into immediate skill creation, existing-skill revision, a named candidate, continued observation, settlement, or retirement. Applies when materially meaningful work exposes a reusable collaboration affordance, an upcoming skill receives new evidence, or skill recursion needs a release decision.

skills.name: collaboration-runbook-authoring
skills.description: Converts a settled, repeatable multi-phase collaboration route into a versioned AI-legible runbook with explicit entry, authority, checks, recovery, stop, and handback. Applies when a known procedure spans several source owners, Issues, or bounded support returns and the runbook plus its linked current owners should provide sufficient re-entry orientation.

skills.name: context-canvas-css-ownership
skills.description: Establishes legible Context Canvas CSS ownership. Applies when expanded.css, cascade diagnosis, selector or token migration, route bundles, first-paint work, or Visual Fidelity Contract mapping enters scope.

skills.name: context-canvas-surface-reading
skills.description: Reads a Context Canvas page or route family as a visitor surface and primary design input. Applies before assessment, planning, or material changes to a Canvas page, embedded instrument, or family relationship.

skills.name: context-canvas-visual-verification
skills.description: Selects proportionate visual and browser evidence for Context Canvas visitor-surface changes. Applies when layout, CSS, responsive behavior, interaction state, print, forced colors, or a visible regression needs review.

skills.name: contextual-jargon-scan
skills.description: Classifies potentially specialist or inside wording within a bounded corpus and revises replaceable shorthand into ordinary language. Applies when public, visitor-facing, or cross-team prose may rely on context its reader does not share, including an in-stride review of material already receiving substantive change.

skills.name: declarative-skill-authoring
skills.description: Authors or revises repository skills as declarative, transferable specifications. Applies when skill metadata, What/When/Boundaries contracts, Rule declarations, optional Given/When/Then examples, conditional context, or experiment-to-helper progression needs definition.

skills.name: evidence-grounded-research-spike
skills.description: Converts current expert writing, official documentation, standards, and practiced experience into a bounded repository decision. Applies when contemporary evidence should change a plan, instruction, architecture boundary, or collaboration method.

skills.name: issue-chain-stewardship
skills.description: Makes related repository issues legible as a revisable work route while each issue retains its own outcome, authority, and acceptance boundary. Applies when completion, evidence, or a human-held decision in one issue materially changes whether another issue can begin or settle.

skills.name: locator-boundary-stewardship
skills.description: Produces locator-safe public collaboration records while exact gated lineage remains recoverable through stable semantic keys and an authorized resolver. Applies when Issues, pull requests, Threadkeeping, handoffs, or public-history preparation cross publication boundaries.

skills.name: practitioner-probe
skills.description: Converts an ambiguous codebase concern, issue, or plausible-but-shallow implementation into a decision-changing technical probe. Applies when mechanism, affected actor, evidence, or instruction yield remains unclear.

skills.name: repository-attribution-stewardship
skills.description: Distinguishes and aligns copyright-holder records, citation metadata, contribution credit, copy-local public notices, and bounded machine projections. Applies during repository attribution changes, fork or adaptation guidance, and cold-start attribution orientation. Legal interpretation and rights decisions remain with a named human receiver or qualified counsel.

skills.name: repository-reentry
skills.description: Reconstructs current truth across source, Git, GitHub, planning, and threadkeeping. Applies during resumed work, handoffs, status reconciliation, stale-plan review, and branch or pull-request re-entry.

skills.name: schema-contract-authoring
skills.description: Authors or revises repository schema families as bounded, legible contracts with distinct identity, authority, retrieval, examples, semantic context, dependency closure, and proportional material-use checks. Applies when a schema root, versioned contract, JSON-LD context, example family, publication route, or cross-repository schema projection enters scope.

skills.name: secret-boundary-inspection
skills.description: Produces a canary-proven, scope-explicit secret-material observation for a repository, exact proposed index, locally available history, or named artifact. Applies before snapshot, publication, delivery, or receiving-repository handoffs where credential-shaped material could travel.

skills.name: source-authority-mapping
skills.description: Traces a claim, artifact, or contract through semantic ownership, source location, projections, delivery routes, receiving use, and promotion. Applies when repositories, workspaces, mirrors, snapshots, or publication surfaces make authority and lineage difficult to distinguish.

skills.name: stateful-artifact-behavior-contracts
skills.description: Designs focused executable behavior contracts for stateful artifacts and prototypes. Applies when owned state crosses import, edit, rendered, export, machine-readable, or recovery boundaries and a consequential regression needs the smallest source-grounded observation.
